prerequisites: Basic knowledge of office automation tools and/or Matlab

learning_outcomes.text: Identify the different technologies for harnessing marine energy resources.
Calculate the energy potential of a given marine location.
Design the optimal type of energy harvesting for a given marine location.
Ability to solve problems in new or unfamiliar environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
The ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.

The ability for autonomous learning that allows continued study through the development of the capacity to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation.
Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and deal with the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students have the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.
Ability to identify, analyze and evaluate the basic dominant phenomena in fluid-mechanical processes and energy transfer and utilization in engineering and industry.
Fundamental analysis of fluid-mechanical and thermal problems of interest in the energy industry, identifying strong and weak variables and evaluating possible simplifying hypotheses.
Performing elementary calculations for sizing, selection of machines and equipment, and operation for installations with fluids with energy transfers.
Ability to study and propose and apply different types of technologies to improve the use and energy efficiency of installations or plants, comparing alternatives by performance and costs.

syllabus_topics: Floating body systems, oscillating water column, overtopping systems
Unit 3: Marine current energy harvesting technologies
Unit 4: Thermal and salinity gradient harvesting technology
Classroom practices: Practical questions related to energy potential calculations or simple power generation analysis of some technologies.
Laboratory practices: Development of a project for the selection and sizing of a turbine for an oscillating water column wave system.
assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, the final exam (EF) accounts for 60% and seminars/activities (S) for 40%. A minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 is required on the final exam; if the exam score is below 3.5, the subject is failed, and the final grade will be the exam score. If EF > 3.5, the final grade is 0.6 * EF + 0.4 * S. For extraordinary calls, the criteria are the same; if no complementary activities were done, the exam counts for 60% with a maximum achievable grade of 6.0 points. For differentiated evaluation, a single written exam accounts for 100% of the final grade.
